title: Robust T-Loss for Medical Image Segmentation
mechanism: Negative log-likelihood of a Student-t on the per-pixel residual. A learnable degrees-of-freedom parameter sets how far large residuals (likely label errors) are down-weighted.
adaptation: Drop-in on the crack channel (one-vs-rest), replacing or adding to CE + Dice, with nu learnt per class. Keep CE for the 22 structural classes. Check that it does not down-weight genuine low-contrast cracks (7% of components).
min_experiment: Arm: house with T-Loss on crack, a 2-seed screen, then 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metrics: crack IoU, relF1@2, components found. Kill if both crack IoU and relF1@2 show no detectable difference after 5 v 5.
evidence: R (abstract): beats traditional losses on Dice for ISIC skin lesions and the Shenzhen lung set under simulated mask noise. Blobby targets, not thin ones.
prior_overlap: none. Robust-loss families are not in section 5; offset-tolerant CE and Dice variants are different mechanisms.

alt_notes.adaptation: Replace CE on crack and inactive with T-Loss (separate learnable nu per class), keep soft Dice.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house with T-Loss, 3 seeds on 5-fold CV. Baseline: house folds. Metric: fold-mean crack IoU. Promote if >= +0.01. About 15 GPU-h.
